seo.title: Terms of Use - SSW EagleEye
seo.description: Terms for using SSW EagleEye, an Azure Managed Application that runs in your own subscription. Draft for legal review.

pageBlocks.headline: Draft for legal review
pageBlocks.text: This page has not yet been reviewed by SSW's legal advisers. It describes how EagleEye actually works today, but it is not a binding agreement until that review is complete and this notice is removed.

pageBlocks.body:
## 1. Who these terms are between

These terms are between SSW (Superior Software for Windows Pty Ltd, ABN to be confirmed, of Level 1, 81-91 Military Road, Neutral Bay NSW 2089, Australia), referred to as "SSW", "we" or "us", and the organization that installs SSW EagleEye ("EagleEye", the "Software") from Azure Marketplace, referred to as "you" or the "Customer". By deploying EagleEye you accept these terms on behalf of that organization.

## 2. What EagleEye is

EagleEye is an Azure Managed Application. When you install it, Azure creates a resource group in **your** subscription containing the Portal, the API, the scan jobs, an Azure SQL database, an Azure OpenAI account, a Key Vault and monitoring resources. Three app registrations are created in **your** Entra tenant. The Software reads the mailboxes of an Entra group you choose and, if you connect it, the GitHub organization you choose, and writes its results to the database in your subscription.

SSW does not operate a copy of EagleEye for you, does not host your data, and has no access to your subscription or tenant unless you grant it for a support engagement. The [Security](/security) page lists every data flow.

## 3. Licence

SSW grants you a non-exclusive, non-transferable licence to install and use EagleEye in your own Azure subscriptions for your internal business purposes for as long as these terms are in force. You may not resell or sublicense the Software, offer it as a service to third parties, reverse engineer it except where the law allows, or remove its notices. The Software, its images and templates remain SSW's property.

## 4. Price and the public beta

EagleEye is free during its public beta, which runs until 1 July 2027. Pricing after the beta will be published on the [Pricing](/pricing) page before the beta ends; you will not be charged by SSW without agreeing to a price first.

Azure charges for the resources EagleEye creates in your subscription, including Azure OpenAI usage, and GitHub charges for your GitHub plan. Those costs are yours under your agreements with Microsoft and GitHub.

Each EagleEye release carries a support end date. After that date the release stops scanning until you apply the update that the Portal offers. SSW publishes updates well before a release reaches its end date.

## 5. Your responsibilities

You are responsible for:

* the Azure subscription, the Entra tenant and the Microsoft 365 licences EagleEye runs on, and for the Azure and GitHub costs it incurs;
* deciding which mailboxes are scanned, by choosing the members of the Entra group, and keeping that decision lawful. Scanning staff email is regulated in most jurisdictions; you must have a lawful basis, tell the people whose mail is scanned, and complete any privacy impact assessment or employee consultation your laws require;
* granting, reviewing and revoking the Microsoft Graph permissions listed on the [Security](/security) page, and deleting the Master app after install;
* the tags, rules and prompts you create, and what you do with the reports;
* securing your subscription and tenant: Conditional Access, who is in the Portal group, secret rotation, and keeping the installed release current;
* backups and retention of the database in your subscription.

## 6. SSW's responsibilities

SSW will:

* publish EagleEye releases, including security fixes, through Azure Marketplace and the in-Portal update;
* keep the two SSW-hosted endpoints that installs depend on available (the container image token endpoint and the version manifest), and tell you on the [Support](/support) page when they are not;
* provide support as described on the [Support](/support) page;
* handle any personal information we do receive as described in the [Privacy Policy](/privacy).

## 7. Your data

Your email, directory and GitHub data, and the results EagleEye produces from them, stay in your subscription and remain yours. SSW claims no rights in them and does not receive them. Nothing in EagleEye sends that data to SSW.

When you no longer want EagleEye, delete the managed application or its resource group; this removes the database, Key Vault, logs and app registrations. There is no copy at SSW to delete. Key Vault keeps deleted secrets recoverable for 90 days under Azure's soft-delete policy, inside your subscription.

## 8. Third-party services

EagleEye calls Microsoft Graph, Azure OpenAI and GitHub from your subscription using your credentials and your agreements with those providers. SSW is not a party to those agreements and is not responsible for those services, their availability or how they process data. Azure OpenAI processes AI tag prompts inside your own Azure OpenAI account.

## 9. Availability

EagleEye runs on your Azure subscription, so its availability is governed by Microsoft's Azure service levels and by how you operate the subscription, not by SSW. SSW does not promise an uptime percentage for EagleEye. For the two SSW-hosted endpoints, SSW's response targets are published on the [Support](/support) page; they are targets, not a service level agreement, and no service credits apply during the public beta.

## 10. Beta software and warranty

EagleEye is beta software, provided "as is". To the extent the law allows, SSW excludes all implied warranties, including fitness for a particular purpose and uninterrupted or error-free operation. AI tags are produced by a language model and can be wrong; review them before you act on them. Nothing in these terms excludes rights you have under the Australian Consumer Law or other laws that cannot be excluded.

## 11. Liability

To the extent the law allows, SSW is not liable for indirect or consequential loss, loss of profit, loss of data, or business interruption arising from EagleEye, and SSW's total liability under these terms is limited to the amount you paid SSW for EagleEye in the twelve months before the claim, which during the public beta is nil. Where the law implies a guarantee that cannot be excluded, SSW's liability is limited, at SSW's option, to resupplying the Software or paying the cost of resupply.

## 12. Suspension and termination

You can stop using EagleEye at any time by deleting the managed application. SSW can end the licence with 30 days' notice if you breach these terms and do not fix the breach, or at the end of the public beta if you do not accept the published pricing. Sections 7, 10, 11 and 14 survive termination.

## 13. Changes to these terms

SSW may update these terms by publishing a new version on this page with a new "last updated" date, and will give at least 30 days' notice of material changes through the Portal or by email to the contact you provided. Continuing to use EagleEye after the change takes effect means you accept the new terms.

## 14. Governing law

These terms are governed by the laws of New South Wales, Australia, and the parties submit to the non-exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of New South Wales.
